exact_statement: For n>=5, the canonical lex sign f_n=-1 on index<floor(2^n/10) has E(f_n)=psi(2 floor(2^n/10)/2^n), attained exactly at its top three coordinates, and E(f_n)->(17 log2(17)-56)/5, where E=min over relevant i of B_i/Inf_i and psi(d)=2-2d+Phi((1-d)^2,d^2)/d. For m>=5,L=m^2,n=m+L,t=2^L floor(2^m/10)+1, the lex sign has its minimum at all L+v2(floor(2^m/10)) newly relevant terminal coordinates; with d0=2^(1-L) its minimum lies between 2-2d0 and 2+d0(6L+8), hence tends to 2 although t/2^n->1/10. For raw recursion F_0=x, F_d=f_5(F_(d-1),...,F_(d-1)) on disjoint copies of f_5=-1 on indices 0,1,2 with +1 child encoded as bit 0, the explicit T,B,T,B,... coordinate path has B_i/Inf_i<3 for every d>=1. Thus E(F_d)<3 for all depths; the proof does not assert monotonicity of E with depth.
